last.verdict: Berkshire's profit slipped as GEICO's insurance results weakened, but the company more than doubled its stock buybacks to about $9.6 billion.

takeaways.label: Insurance weakened
takeaways.text: Insurance underwriting profit fell 42.9% to $1.35 billion, mainly on rising GEICO losses and higher expenses, pulling operating earnings down 5.8% to $12.7 billion.

takeaways.label: Buybacks accelerate
takeaways.text: Berkshire repurchased about $9.6 billion of its own stock, more than double the prior quarter, which signals it sees its shares as good value.

takeaways.label: Rail and utilities offset
takeaways.text: BNSF railroad earnings rose 19.3% to $1.73 billion and Berkshire Hathaway Energy rose 8.3%, cushioning the insurance decline.

takeaways.label: Cash pile still huge
takeaways.text: Cash and Treasury bills stood at $377.4 billion despite the larger buybacks. Net earnings fell to $22.1 billion from $30.8 billion a year earlier.

history.verdict: Investors cheered Berkshire finally spending its cash pile on buybacks and stocks.

reasons.label: Big share buybacks
reasons.text: Berkshire bought back about $4.5 billion of its own stock in the quarter, up from small buybacks before.

reasons.label: Cash put to work
reasons.text: Berkshire became a net stock buyer for the first time in about 14 quarters, with a Alphabet stake included.

reasons.label: Stronger operating profit
reasons.text: Operating earnings rose about 16% to $13.0 billion, though insurance underwriting profit slipped to $1.7 billion.
